body:
Thank you for this contribution. This comment tells you what happens next with this PR, and why.

The maintainer decided on 2026-11-18 that the project completes an outside PR when its last author activity is more than 24 hours old. The purpose is to get your work into `main` and not to let it wait behind conflicts. This PR is in that group.

What we do:
- An agent of this repository merges `main` into your branch and corrects the open review findings. Your commits stay as they are. We do not rebase and we do not force-push.
- The agent pushes to your branch, because this PR permits edits by maintainers.
- A different agent reviews the result. The PR merges when that review is clean.
- Each step gets a comment on this PR.

If you want to do this work yourself, write a comment here. Then we stop and the PR stays with you.

Merged `origin/main` into this branch at the maintainer's order of 2026-11-18. New head: `6b86583ee317f9cf1b23706d545af8566d940287`. There is no force-push and no rebase.

Hand-resolved hunk:
- `crates/tools/src/tools.rs`, `Tool::is_sane`. This branch moved the law to `tool_sanity.rs`. Main (#2011) added `ToolKind::Wire` to the old inline body. The resolution keeps this branch's body: `self.why_not_sane().is_none()`.

Ported rules (from main into `crates/tools/src/tool_sanity.rs`):
- Wire is one of the kinds that turn no spindle (`Torch | Electrode | Waterjet | Wire`), line 67. A wire with rpm other than 0 gets "a wire turns no spindle: its spindle speed must be 0, not N rpm".
- The kind arm `ToolKind::Wire => crate::wire::refusal(self)`, line 155. It gives the wire's own words for the diameter range, the corner radius and the cutting rows.
- No other rule that main added to `crates/tools/src/` since the merge base `a529c4553` touches `is_sane`. Main's cutting-row change (`cutting_rows::refusal_for_kind` refuses rows on a wire) runs through the existing call.

Decision: keep the structure of this PR and port the two Wire rules. A plain take of one side is dropped: this branch's side loses the wire law, and main's side loses the named refusals. The entry is in `docs/decisions/1186-tool-refusal-names.md`.

Tests:
- `tool_sanity_tests.rs`: the oracle has main's two Wire lines, and `KINDS` has 18 kinds (17 before).
- New pins: `tool_sanity::tests::a_bad_wire_is_named` and `tool_sanity::tests::a_valid_wire_is_accepted`.
- A fix in `crates/app/tests/project_tool_refusal.rs`: the two tests used one temp file and ran in parallel. One test removed the file while the other read it. Each call now has its own file.

Gate:
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`, 52 steps on merge commit `900f138e0`: 51 ok, 1 failed (`project_tool_refusal`, the temp-file race above).
- After the fix, `project_tool_refusal` passed 3 times with 6 test threads.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-tools --no-deps --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

The PR stays a draft with `conflicts`. A delta review of the merge is necessary (`/resolve-conflicts check`).

<!-- pr-reviewer: 6b86583ee317f9cf1b23706d545af8566d940287 -->
**Verdict: no blockers**

Full review under the safety floor (the tool validity law moves to a new file). Read from the diff. Not built.

## 1. Rule-by-rule equivalence with main's `Tool::is_sane`

I compared `git show origin/main:crates/tools/src/tools.rs` (`is_sane`, all kinds, Wire included) with `crates/tools/src/tool_sanity.rs` at this head. Each rule is present, with the same bound:

| Rule on main | `tool_sanity.rs` |
|---|---|
| 14 fields finite | 16-34 (same 14 fields) |
| `diameter > 0 && <= 500` | 36-38 |
| `corner_r >= 0`, `<= diameter * 0.5` | 39-44 |
| `tip_angle < 180` | 45-47 |
| `pitch, pitch_min, nose_radius, width, shank_d, shank_len, holder_d, holder_len >= 0` | 48-60 |
| `flute_len > 0` | 61-63 |
| rpm == 0 for Torch / Electrode / Waterjet / Wire, else rpm > 0 | 64-73 (Wire included) |
| `feed > 0` | 74-76 |
| flutes 1..=32 | 77-79 |
| `orientation::is_valid` (1..=9) | 80-82 |
| `catalog.refusal()` | 85-87 |
| `cutting_rows::refusal_for_kind` | 88-90 |
| `TurningData::is_sane` and `rpm <= max_rpm` | 93-100, 198-217 |
| Drill `tip_angle > 60` | 111 |
| Tap `pitch > 0` | 112 |
| Turning nose `> 0 && <= d/2` | 115 |
| Groove width `> 0 && < d` | 120 |
| Thread width and angle | 124, 127 (two guarded arms; a failed guard falls through correctly) |
| Form width, crown, `w <= 2r` | 131, 134, 135 |
| Taper `tip_angle > 0` | 139 |
| Probe ball and stylus | 141, 145 |
| Torch `corner_r == 0` | 149 |
| Waterjet `waterjet::refusal` | 152 |
| Wire `wire::refusal` | 155 |
| Electrode `electrode::is_sane` (width finite, `0 < w <= MAX_SIDE` = 500, corner 0, outline record) | 156, 164-173 |
| ThreadMill / ThreadMillSingle `thread_mill::is_sane` (form, core, pitches) | 157, 177-195 |

- The old law is one conjunction. Thus the order of the checks changes only which message comes first, never the verdict.
- Each negated compare (`x <= 0` for `!(x > 0)`) runs after the finite check. Thus NaN cannot pass a negated compare. NaN and infinity in each of the 14 fields are refused at line 32, and NaN in turning data is refused at 203-213.
- Main has no change in `crates/tools/src` after the merge base `ee49b0680` (`git diff ee49b0680 origin/main -- crates/tools/src` is empty). The ported Wire rules are current.
- The remerge-diff of `900f138e0` resolves only the `is_sane` body in `tools.rs`, to `self.why_not_sane().is_none()`. No other hunk was resolved by hand.

## 2. Callers

- `AddTool`, `ChangeTool` (`crates/app/src/commands/tool.rs:112, 233`), `ImportTools` (`tool_import.rs:223`), the project loader (`project/validate.rs:170`) and `parse_tool_library` (`tool_library.rs:159`) refuse on `Some(why)`. This is the same set of tools that `!is_sane()` refused. Only the message is new.
- `torch_refusal` still runs first in the commands. That order is unchanged.
- All other callers of `Tool::is_sane` and `TurningData::is_sane` keep the same boolean, because each is now `why_not_sane().is_none()`.
- No caller ignores a refusal. No other code or test reads the old texts ("finite and positive", "parameters are not usable") for a tool.

## 3. Messages and Prime Directive

- Each message names the tool (`tool '<name>': ...`) and the field and bound in plain words. The `ToolDto` / `Tool` debug dump is gone.
- No `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic!` outside tests.
- `ToolKind` has a `Display` arm for each kind, so line 69 says "a wire turns no spindle ...".

## 4. Tests

- `the_named_law_gives_the_old_verdict_everywhere` (`tool_sanity_tests.rs:128`) holds main's body as the oracle (lines 23-98, Wire lines included). It sweeps every catalog tool as each of the 18 kinds, with 13 edge values in each of the 14 fields, plus flutes, orientation and turning data. `agree` checks `why_not_sane` and `is_sane` against the oracle. This is a real old-against-new run.
- `a_bad_wire_is_named` pins the rpm rule, the diameter range and the corner radius, each with its message. `a_valid_wire_is_accepted` pins the two range ends and 0.25 mm.
- `crates/app/tests/project_tool_refusal.rs` imports `camcraft_app::project`, so it is in the correct crate. It has its Gate map and lane lines.
- The temp-file fix is sound: the path has the process id and an atomic counter, so two parallel tests cannot share one file.

## 5. Shape and records

- `tool_sanity.rs` has 221 lines and `tool_sanity_tests.rs` has 233 lines. Both have a provenance line. `tools.rs` goes from 714 to 614 lines. It was over 400 lines before this PR.
- The decision file has Chosen, Why and Dropped entries for each choice, the two merges included.
- The PR body has `Changelog:`, `Fixes #1186`, the pinning tests and a "Not exercised" section.

## Non-blocking findings

1. **Catch-all in the kind law** (`crates/tools/src/tool_sanity.rs:158`, `_ => None`). A new `ToolKind` added later gets no kind rule and is accepted without a refusal. Main's `_ => true` did the same, so this is not a regression. The equivalence test does not find such a gap, because `KINDS` (`tool_sanity_tests.rs:100`) is a list written by hand and the oracle also has `_ => true`. Recommendation: replace the catch-all with an exhaustive match (`ToolKind::EndMill | ToolKind::BallNose | ToolKind::BullNose | ToolKind::Bore => None`, and an explicit `None` arm for each guarded kind). Then the compiler stops a new kind that has no decision. This can be a `P7` follow-up.
2. **Gate record is not on the final head.** The body records the quick gate on `dbf7799e`. The head is `6b86583e`, after the merge of main and the temp-file fix. Before the PR is flagged ready, record a green quick gate on `6b86583e` for `camcraft-tools` (lib tests, `tool_sanity`) and for `camcraft-app` (`project_tool_refusal`, `tool_cutter_params`, the `tool_*` suites).
3. **Effort label.** The body says `effort:low`. The change rewrites the law that accepts or refuses a tool, which is under the safety floor. Think about `effort:high` on #1186, so that the review tier is correct.
4. **`conflicts` label is stale.** `git merge-tree` of this head with `origin/main` (`b48c6582`) is clean. The label can be removed at the next re-check.

Merge note. Class: DELTA (one conflict resolved by hand in `Tool::is_sane`, by the maintainer's decision of 2026-11-18 to port the Wire rules). This merge relies on the full review of head `6b86583ee317f9cf1b23706d545af8566d940287` in comment 6977230739 (no blockers). The quick gate ran on merge commit `900f138e0` (51 of 52 steps ok). The one failed binary, `project_tool_refusal`, passed after the test-only fix. The non-blocking findings go to a follow-up issue.
